articleBlocks: At first, this looked more like parts of a car than the real category.
Barrel pushed me in that direction immediately.
Spring kept that theory alive for a moment, but ink chamber still did not quite fit.
That was the moment the first idea stopped working.
Then Ink chamber made me stop thinking about parts of a car and start thinking about the real category.
Barrel made sense as a pen barrel.
Spring made sense as a pen spring.
The answer was Parts of a pen.
Cap and Ink chamber then felt less surprising and more like the last pieces falling into place.
Looking back, the answer feels obvious in the best way.
solutionNarrative: Barrel and Spring first pulled me toward parts of a car, so that was the first path I tested. It held together for a moment, but ink chamber never really fit it. The more I pushed that first read, the more the board sounded stitched together instead of naturally solved.

The solve turned when I stopped treating ink chamber as just another clue and asked what kind of thing each clue could really be describing. Once I made that shift, I was no longer thinking about parts of a car; I was checking whether the earlier clues all behaved like parts of the same real set. That was when the answer became clear, because the remaining clues stopped feeling like separate trivia and started reinforcing the real category.
